papers.title: Tuning High-Voltage Cu–Fe Redox in P2-Type Layered Metal Oxide Cathodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract P2-type layered oxides have gained significant attention in energy storage applications due to their superior rate capability and cycling performance. However, P2-type layered oxides suffer from low sodium content and irreversible phase transitions at high voltages, limiting reversible capacity and long-term durability. Although Cu–Mn-based systems offer a high operating voltage through the Cu2+/Cu3+ redox couple, the accessible voltage window remains narrow, resulting in restricted capacity. In this work, we employ a compositional engineering strategy by introducing Fe into the Cu–Mn framework to enhance both structural stability and redox activity. Fe incorporation enhances structural stability and redox activity by introducing additional cationic redox centers. The synergistic involvement of the Cu2+/Cu3+ and Fe3+/Fe4+ redox couples maintains a high average voltage (∼3.54 V) while improving electrochemical reversibility. The resulting P2–Na0.7Cu0.3Mn0.6Fe0.1O2 cathode demonstrates a reversible capacity exceeding ∼90 mAh g–1 when combined with CNTs, along with excellent cycling stability. Ex situ XRD analysis reveals reversible phase evolution, confirming enhanced structural robustness during cycling. This study highlights the effectiveness of Fe substitution in optimizing Cu–Mn cathode chemistry, offering a promising pathway for high-energy and durable sodium-ion battery systems.

papers.title: Compositional Uniformity and Thermal Properties of Tetra- N -butyl Ammonium Bromide and Tetra- N -butyl Ammonium Chloride Mixed Semiclathrate Hydrates
papers.abstract: Abstract Mixed semiclathrate hydrates (SCHs) incorporating various guest molecules exhibit high latent heat and allow precise control of the melting temperatures, making them promising materials for cold energy storage applications. The compositional uniformity and thermal properties of tetra-n-butylammonium bromide (TBAB) + tetra-n-butylammonium chloride (TBAC) mixed SCHs were evaluated via dual-energy X-ray computer tomography (DECT), microdifferential scanning calorimetry (μDSC), digital microscopy, and ion chromatography. DECT indicated that the tetragonal mixed SCHs are homogeneous solids, whereas the orthorhombic mixed SCHs with high or low-Br content are heterogeneous. The DSC curve of the tetragonal mixed SCHs exhibited a single endothermic peak, whereas those of the orthorhombic mixed SCHs showed split peaks. The orthorhombic mixed SCH dissociated in two stages, consistent with the split DSC peaks. The Br– content of the orthorhombic mixed SCH was higher than that of tetragonal SCH. The orthorhombic mixed SCHs exhibit high latent heats (227–231 J g–1) as phase change materials, with melting temperatures around 283–285 K. These values are higher than other SCHs formed from a single guest molecule with melting temperatures below 289 K, making them suitable for cold energy storage in air-conditioning systems.

papers.title: Self-Assembled Oxide Nanoneedle-Induced Strain for Tunable Excitonic Emission in Monolayer MoS2
papers.abstract: Abstract Strain engineering has emerged as a powerful approach for tailoring the optical response of two-dimensional semiconductors. In this work, we show that monolayer MoS2 exhibits tunable excitonic emission, when nanoneedle-like oxide protrusions form across the monolayer surface during a photo-oxidation-assisted exfoliation process. These protrusions locally deform the lattice, generating spatially varying strain fields within the MoS2 layer. Photoluminescence and Raman measurements reveal a clear correlation between strained regions, exciton peak shifts, and enhanced emission, with the photoluminescence intensity increasing by approximately 3-fold, accompanied by a red shift of the in-plane (E2g1) vibrational mode, indicative of strain. Furthermore, selected monolayers and unexfoliated regions exhibit additional emergent near-infrared photoluminescence features absent in pristine MoS2. Unlike conventional strain-engineering approaches requiring external mechanical deformation, specialized substrate prepatterning, or complex heterostructures, this simple one-step process generates intrinsic nanoneedle-induced strain, providing an effective route for tailoring excitonic recombination and extending the optical response of monolayer TMDCs.

papers.title: Experimental Study on Methane Explosion Suppression in Pipelines by Mixed Systems of Inert Gases (CO2/N2) and HFC-227ea
papers.abstract: Abstract To address the high inert gas demand and cost of heptafluoropropane (HFC-227ea) in gas explosion prevention, a custom-built pipeline experimental platform was employed to investigate the suppression effects of CO2, N2, and HFC-227ea on 9.5% methane explosions. A BOPP film separated the explosion and suppression zones to simulate nonpremixed conditions. The peak overpressure and average flame propagation speed were analyzed to evaluate suppression characteristics and the influence of film-breaking. Results show that CO2 outperforms N2 at equal volume fractions; both achieve the optimal suppression effect within the tested concentration range at 40%, reducing the peak overpressure by 25.8% and 24.4% and the flame speed by 40.1% and 34.0%, respectively. HFC-227ea exhibits strong chemical inhibition at low concentrations (2–8%), achieving 51.4% flame speed reduction at 8%. In mixtures with the total concentration fixed at 40%, suppression performance improves with higher HFC-227ea proportion. The 32% CO2/8% HFC-227ea mixture reduces the peak overpressure by 35.3% and the flame speed by 62.9%, outperforming pure CO2 at the same total concentration. No marked synergy is observed at low HFC-227ea ratios, likely due to film-breaking effects induced by BOPP membrane rupture. These findings provide theoretical and technical support for optimizing explosion suppression media in confined industrial spaces, suggesting a potentially cost-effective solution for engineering applications.

papers.title: Counterion-Mediated Humidity Modulation of Electronic Transport in Pristine MWCNT/TOCNF Composites
papers.abstract: Abstract Humidity-driven electrical responses in carbon-cellulose composites are commonly attributed to matrix swelling. However, in TEMPO-oxidized nanocellulose (TOCNF), water uptake also releases Na+ counterions from carboxylate residues, enabling interfacial polarization via image-charge interactions that can modulate junction-limited electronic transport. Here, we formulate aqueous inks in which TOCNF disperses pristine (nonfunctionalized) multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNT) without covalent modification, yielding homogeneous, spray-processable composite films. Using DC electrical measurements under controlled relative humidity, impedance spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, and a mean-field electrostatic model for counterion-mediated polarization, we show that percolated TOCNF/MWCNT films exhibit reproducible resistance gains, reaching up to ∼270%, that are inconsistent with a swelling mechanism alone. To support this view, a control based on nonoxidized nanocellulose (with a negligible amount of dissociable counterions) was designed, which shows only modest changes at high humidity, thereby sustaining an important, counterion-mediated interfacial route. The impedance data indicate predominantly electronic transport and a humidity-dependent low-frequency reactive response near the percolation threshold. The DC measurements establish a reproducible steady-state behavior and within-session cycling, while intrinsic response times and long-term stability remain to be more explored. The model rationalizes how increased counterion concentration under humidification can induce polarizing charges at the nanotube surface, driving electrostatic repulsion and relative reorientation that weaken conductive CNT-CNT junctions across the network. Invoking the Derjaguin approximation, an effective, counterion-induced repulsive interaction between CNT surfaces is computed, which prevents the building-up of large connecting junctions across the network, thus reducing their ability to assemble percolating pathways. These findings establish an overlooked counterion-mediated design principle to tune mixed ionic-electronic transport in sustainable CNT/nanocellulose electronic composites operating under humid or electrolyte-adjacent conditions.
